neighbours.label: A verb of periodic rotation or recurrence among hosts or turns ('rotate', 'alternate') after an adverb in an institutional schedule, vs the same schedules described with a non-recurrence verb
fire: Under the treaty the chairmanship would annually rotate among the member states.
The founders agreed the festival would regularly rotate between three coastal towns.
From then on the summit would internationally rotate and take place every two years.
Club rules say the captaincy will seasonally rotate among the senior players.
Delegates decided that the conference should periodically rotate across continents.
Since 1990 the trophy final has continued to yearly alternate between the two capitals.
The bylaws state that the presidency must annually rotate between the two parties.
Organisers hoped the exhibition would eventually rotate through every major museum.
quiet: Under the treaty the chairmanship would be held by the largest member state.
The founders agreed the festival would remain in the first coastal town.
From then on the summit would be hosted in Geneva and take place every two years.
Club rules say the captaincy will be given to the oldest senior player.
Delegates decided that the conference should stay in Vienna for good.
Since 1990 the trophy final has continued to be played in the old capital.
The bylaws state that the presidency must belong to the founding party.
Organisers hoped the exhibition would eventually settle in one major museum.

predictions: Weak: rotation verbs may reach 0.1-0.3; non-recurrence twins under 0.05. Expected to fail.
